text: Giorgi Sharashidze - What talk is there of Vice-Prime Ministership or State Ministership, they aren't even giving him a proper office, he won't have a staff and won't have a secretary - I would advise Mdinaradze not to get too fixated on this office either and to work remotely (28.04.2026, 12:04)

"What Vice-Prime Ministership or State Ministership are we talking about? They aren't even giving him a proper office; Mdinaradze won't even have a staff or a secretary. I would advise him not to get too fixated on this office and to work remotely from home," stated Giorgi Sharashidze, an MP from the "Gakharia for Georgia" party, while discussing the creation of the position of State Minister for the coordination of law enforcement agencies. 

According to him, appointing a general-coordinator will change nothing except that it will be his "temporary satisfaction and a way to send him into retirement."

"The planned changes have nothing to do with solving the problems of our country's citizens or Georgia's security issues. This is yet another manifestation of informal governance. 'Dream' and the 89 deputies sitting in parliament have no role other than to simply 'legitimize' Ivanishvili's decisions, which are never coordinated with them. What talk is there of a vice-premiership or a state ministry? They aren't even giving Mdinaradze a proper office; he won't have a staff or even a secretary. I would advise him not to get too fixated on this office and just work remotely from home instead."

If coordination is so important, the head of the State Security Service is not dismissed after six months for the sake of coordination. The head of the State Security Service is not appointed for a six-year term by chance—this provision in the law is not there by accident. We see that two heads of the State Security Service have already been replaced in the last year. This points to an unstable environment and informal governance. A person was granted the rank of general in the morning and demoted to a coordinator by the evening—what special expectations should we have of this person?

"As for the coordinatorship — 'Dream' itself introduced this term, and yesterday, when one of our leaders, Giga Parulava, at the Legal Committee meeting, was stating the fact that you are appointing [him] as a coordinator, it was met with such irritation that they criticized his vocabulary and tone. This 'coordinator' is a term introduced by 'Dream,' and if it is offensive to them, then let them explain where they got this term from in the first place. Therefore, when we say that this appointment of a general-coordinator will change nothing except that it will simply be a way to temporarily satisfy him and send him into retirement, this is the reality," Sharashidze stated.

For information, the Parliament is considering a draft law through an expedited procedure, on the basis of which the position of State Minister for the Coordination of Law Enforcement Agencies is being introduced within the Government of Georgia.
According to the draft, the Administration of the Government shall provide logistical and organizational support for the activities of the new State Minister.

According to the Parliamentary Secretary of the Government, Vakhtang Bachiashvili, the powers of the State Minister will be specified in a government decree, where their routine and strategic responsibilities will be outlined.
Mamuka Mdinaradze will be appointed to the position of State Minister for Coordination of Law Enforcement Agencies.
